method: File metadata: iPhone created/modified = recording start/end, Android filename = recording initiated and created/modified = file finalised (about the end); second resolution, which gives a feasible start window per clip.

Audio: GCC-PHAT (150-3500 Hz) cross-correlation of the clips' audio, restricted to the lag window the metadata allows; three-clip takes are solved jointly (offsets must satisfy d13 = d12 + d23) and tested against the same search on shifted windows.
Audio start is within 40 ms of video start in every file (Android audio 16-38 ms later; that lead is subtracted).
Not frame-exact: see the per-take uncertainty.

take4.label: case 4, 14:18
take4.method: joint triangle-constrained GCC-PHAT inside the file-metadata windows (p=0.003 against shifted searches)
take4.note: cam2-cam3 correlation is very strong (z=33) and cam1-cam3 agrees; the direct cam1-cam2 pair peaks 0.57 s away, so cam2 against cam1 may be off by up to 0.6 s.
take4.offsets_relative_to: the take's earliest clip start (offsets are start_offset_used_s)

evidence.caveat: The three strongest pair peaks are not mutually consistent (they miss the triangle by 0.57 s). The solution keeps cam2-cam3 (z 33) and cam1-cam3 (inside the iPhone metadata window 4.85-5.36 s) and gives up the direct cam1-cam2 peak.

take5.offsets_relative_to: the take's earliest clip start (offsets are start_offset_used_s)

take7_8.note: clip starts are the midpoints of the metadata windows: about +-0.5 s between iPhone clips, +-1.1 s for the Android clips. Treat multi-camera cases of this take as approximately synchronised only.
